opening_message:
Ticket 1: Diana Cooper (employee ID E020) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E020.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Diana Cooper (E020) is a full-time Engineer requesting admin access to Source Code. Since Engineers own Source Code, full-time employees in the owning role may have admin. Recommend granting admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Diana Cooper (E020) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors never exceed read without advanced training. Requested admin is above the maximum, so grant read.
reason: Diana Cooper (E020) requested admin access to Source Code. The two notes conflict on employment type: HR's database shows full_time, while Security's database (also verified at write time) shows contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training, and never admin. Because the contractor classification is present in the Security database and the rule that contractors never receive admin is absolute, admin cannot be granted. The requested admin exceeds the contractor maximum, so I grant the maximum permitted: read.
